- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for early periods.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 5x historical mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 2x prior peak or 3x recent average.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 10–20% to forecast for 3–5 days ahead.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.33–1.00), model exhibits erratic behavior; smooth forecast using 3-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply 50% discount to forecast if sentiment drops below 0.33 in last 3 days.
- If history shows mean reversion (price oscillates around 2.0–2.5), model tends to overpredict; use 20–30% downward bias for 10–15 day forecasts.
- When sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.33) and price is falling, model often fails to recognize trend reversal; add 10–20% upward bias if sentiment turns positive within 3 days.
